notes.body: Bōya literally means 'little boy,' but here it is a fond, generic way to call a baby: the narrator has already said the child is a girl. The English keeps the Japanese word so as not to fix what the parents leave unfixed.
Gohan means both cooked rice and a meal. Here the steam and serving from the pot mark it as freshly cooked rice, the warm staple set against the cold potato to come.

data.say: Two Curious-only notes for p8, Bōya and gohan as first-use keeps; no Casual note and no storm or table note since context already supplies them.
